desc.en: Adds up the numbers on its two ways in, plus 1 when its “start” port is “yes”. A “—” is left out; with nothing to add, it outputs “—”.
Every cell must come after the cells it reads. Reverse the order, and the directions the circuit reads must reverse too.
Takes the smallest of up to three ways in (when its “start” port is “yes”, 0 counts as a way in too), then adds this cell’s cost. When every way in is “—”, it outputs “—”.
Copy the table into several layers, so the state remembers one more thing that affects the future.
One word along the top, the other down the left. If the letters match, up-left + 1; otherwise the larger of up and left.
Outputs the smallest of: the smallest of up, left and up-left, plus 1; up-left itself when the letters match; 0 on the start.
Outputs the larger of “keep” and “swap for” plus “plus”.
Keep just one row and rewrite it in place. The direction you rewrite in decides how many times each item can be used.
Reads the three positions the opponent could face: if any of them is a loss, this cell is a win; otherwise a loss.
Reads a whole run of cells at once. But sweeping from the start on every cell is slow: if the previous cell has already stored the answer, use it instead of sweeping again.
If some earlier position can be split and the piece from there to here is exactly a word, this position can be split too.
Its left and right parts are two runs of numbers: it adds them split point by split point, takes the smallest, then adds the cost of the whole run.
Any order works, as long as every cell comes after the cells it reads.
Takes the largest of up to four ways in, then multiplies it by the number set on its part (0.9, say).
When the outcome is uncertain, weight each outcome by how likely it is, then compare.
For every tag in every column, keep the cheapest explanation up to here: each row of the previous column plus its transition cost, then the min.
Anything below 0 is cut to 0: starting afresh beats carrying a negative score along. The answer is the largest cell in the table.
Each cell = its own energy + the smallest of the three cells above it. Trace back from the smallest cell in the bottom row, and cut that seam out.
